name: Battle of Gettysburg

sides.name: Union (Army of the Potomac)
sides.strength: About 93,921 in seven infantry corps and the cavalry corps

sides.name: Confederacy (Army of Northern Virginia)
sides.commander: Robert E. Lee, James Longstreet, A. P. Hill, Richard S. Ewell
sides.strength: About 71,699 in three infantry corps under Longstreet, Hill, and Ewell
sides.casualties: Around 23,000 to 28,000 killed, wounded, or missing

summary: Lee's second invasion of the North met Meade's Army of the Potomac at the road junction of Gettysburg. The first day forced the Union back through the town to the high ground south of it. The second day produced the famous fights at Devil's Den, Little Round Top, the Wheatfield, and Culp's Hill as Lee tried to envelop both Union flanks. On the third day Lee ordered the frontal attack on Cemetery Ridge known to history as Pickett's Charge. Around 12,500 Confederates crossed three quarters of a mile of open ground under artillery and rifle fire. Barely half came back. Lee retreated to Virginia the next night.
significance: Gettysburg was the high-water mark of the Confederacy. Combined with Vicksburg's fall on the fourth of July, the twin defeats reset the Civil War's strategic balance. The Army of Northern Virginia would not invade the North again. Four months later Abraham Lincoln stood at the new soldiers' cemetery and delivered the Gettysburg Address, redefining the war's meaning around the principle that all men are created equal.
